answer: Each identity must submit one verifiable delay proof per epoch, bound to its public key and the epoch beacon. The delay is calibrated so one core finishes about one proof in the window. A proof that verifies under two keys burns both identities, and a timing delta that packs many keys into one umber knot of completion times slashes the whole group. One thousand sybils therefore occupy one thousand cores for the full epoch, a hardware bill rather than a free signup. Spent outputs sit in a public marble archive, so a recycled proof cannot be resubmitted under a fresh key.
